**Şadi Evren Şeker** teaches artificial intelligence and computer science at the university level in the United States and has taught in Türkiye.

He earned a Ph.D. in computer engineering from Yıldız Technical University in 2010, after studying computer science and engineering at Yeditepe University and Istanbul Technical University. He has worked in artificial intelligence and machine learning for more than 25 years. He was a visiting professor of computer science at Smith College in 2016–2017. In Türkiye he became an associate professor of management information systems in 2015 and a full professor in 2020; he chaired the Department of Business Administration at Istanbul Medeniyet University (2014–2015) and later served as dean of the Faculty of Computer and Information Technologies at Istanbul University.

His published work includes research on a computerized argument Delphi technique (*IEEE Access*, 2015), a study of large language models in software development (*Electrica*, 2026), books on business intelligence and data mining, and many Turkish-language entries in *YBS Ansiklopedi*, the management information systems encyclopedia whose entries appear in this book's From the Field sections. He develops HermAI, an open-source Python package for hermeneutic explainable AI, presented in a published article with Arslanhan (Şeker & Arslanhan, 2026, *Artificial Intelligence Theory and Applications*, 6(1), 56–74), and holds four patents. For many years he has taught computer science to a wide audience through the *Bilgisayar Kavramları* (Computer Concepts) YouTube channel, which had more than 280,000 subscribers in October 2026.

He is a founder of OptiWisdom, which develops Compass, this book's optional digital companion, and software for businesses, including AI tools, and the founder of Bilkav Eğitim Danışmanlık ("How This Book Was Written" declares these interests).
